conflicts.question: How often should MGUS be monitored in primary care?

source_positions.position: Repeat at around 6 months after diagnosis, then reduce frequency if stable; low-risk patients may move to long interval monitoring or no routine follow-up in selected older/frail patients.
Check every 3 to 4 months for the first year, then every 6 to 12 months if no symptoms develop.

conflicts.resolution: Use a conservative primary-care review approach: repeat at 3 to 6 months to confirm stability, then annually if stable unless local haematology approves longer intervals. Record that local D&G haematology should confirm whether low-risk patients can move to 2 to 3 yearly or symptom-triggered review.

conflicts.question: Should raised paraprotein alone be a cancer referral?

source_positions.position: Raised paraprotein without CRAB or other USC features should not be referred as USC.
Certain paraprotein level/sFLC thresholds should trigger haematology assessment even without CRAB features.

conflicts.resolution: Separate urgency: do not use USOC for isolated paraprotein without CRAB, but refer by routine or urgent non-cancer haematology route when MGUS risk thresholds or changing results are present.
conflicts.publication_note: Local route name and urgency should be confirmed.

conflicts.question: Can normal blood tests exclude myeloma?

source_positions.position: Normal initial blood tests make myeloma unlikely in primary-care assessment.
No single serum or urine paraprotein/light-chain test alone should exclude myeloma.

conflicts.resolution: State that a normal combined initial assessment makes myeloma less likely, but persistent concerning symptoms need safety-netting, repeat testing, and specialist discussion/referral if clinical concern remains.

summary: Main conflict is MGUS monitoring intensity.
Referral wording should distinguish USOC cancer referral from non-cancer haematology advice/referral.
Direct BSH full-paper extraction was limited, so threshold statements require editor/local haematology confirmation.
